_comment: Two independent axes, deliberately not the same flag:
is_optional  — may fail without failing the release (continue-on-error).
publish_wave — 'primary' ships in the first publish; 'backfill' ships in
a second publish after the channel is already promoted.
Nothing is in the backfill wave any more, and adding something back needs
a better reason than the original one. The wave existed because macOS
Intel took 33-63 min against a 25-31 min required path over v0.3.70-73.
That gap decayed: measured from the published revisions, the second
publish landed 20.4 min after the first on v0.3.80, 8.1 on v0.3.78, 4.9
It was not free. Every release produced two revisions, and the second
promotion — a manual step — was missed on three of the last ten stable
versions, leaving the incomplete revision live and macOS Intel off the
download page. It also put two revisions' asset rows on one spaces_path,
which is what made the notarization callback raise MultipleObjectsReturned
and strand Apple Silicon on v0.4.0.
An optional leg still cannot gate a release: is_optional keeps it
continue-on-error, and the publish jobs list the secondary builds in
`needs` but not in `if`, so a failed one is waited for and then published
without.
